title.en: Universal gates: NAND and NOR, and combinations of gates

hook.en: Chip makers can build an entire processor out of just one kind of gate, the NAND. Every other gate can be made from it.

objectives.en: Give the truth tables of NAND and NOR
Build NOT, AND and OR from NAND gates (and from NOR gates)
Find the output of a combination of gates

narration.en: Chip makers can build an entire processor out of just one kind of gate, the NAND. Every other gate can be made from it.

body.en: NAND is AND followed by NOT: $Y = \overline{A\cdot B}$, 0 only when both inputs are 1. NOR is OR followed by NOT: $Y = \overline{A + B}$, 1 only when both inputs are 0. They are universal: NOT = NAND with inputs joined; AND = NAND followed by a NAND-NOT; OR = NAND of the inverted inputs, since $\overline{\bar A\cdot\bar B} = A + B$ (De Morgan). The same can be done with NOR gates.

points.en: De Morgan: (Ā·B̄)‾ = A + B, (Ā + B̄)‾ = A·B

body.en: A small circle (bubble) on a gate symbol means NOT. NAND = AND with a bubble; NOR = OR with a bubble. Two bubbles in a row cancel.

narration.en: Bubble rule. A small circle (bubble) on a gate symbol means NOT. NAND = AND with a bubble; NOR = OR with a bubble. Two bubbles in a row cancel.

passage.en: A NAND gate gives 0 only when __1__ inputs are 1. Joining the two inputs of a NOR gate makes a __2__ gate. A NAND gate followed by a NOT gate acts as an __3__ gate. NAND and NOR are called __4__ gates.

points.en: NAND = NOT(AND) is 0 only for 1, 1; NOR = NOT(OR) is 1 only for 0, 0.
